title: Track operator mistakes as their own intervention category
summary: Add a `mistake` variant to the closed intervention category list. Status and the audit then count mistakes per class and per cause. Introspection of a mistake proposes the check or knowledge that would have prevented it. The audience is Sri, who wants repeat mistake causes to become Athena work.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for the category, the counts, and the proposal; clippy clean.
Criteria check counts and proposals in output.
The criterion checks that mistakes are visible and become work.
One change on the existing intervention pipeline.
Prefix-marked records are counted too, not only new ones.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The category list is the Rust enum InterventionCategory in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs, with parse and ALL.

'Class' means class_of_work of the affected job. 'Cause' is derived from the mistake record's text or an existing introspection field. If no cause field exists, the producer picks the smallest such field.
Interventions with text starting 'Mistake:' but category `other` count as mistakes, so the back-filled eleven are included. Records stay immutable.
No change to athena.toml or defaults.toml is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: new tests pass. They show that an intervention logged with category `mistake` is accepted by the parser and `InterventionCategory::ALL`, and that an unknown category is still rejected with the list including `mistake`.

Run `cargo test`: a test with several mistake interventions of different classes and causes shows that status and the audit output report mistake counts per class and per cause, and that the JSON has those breakdowns separate from `interventions_by_category`.
Run `cargo test`: a test shows that introspecting a `mistake` intervention produces a proposal naming the check or knowledge that would have prevented it. Repeat causes aggregate into one proposal.

Existing records with category `other` and text starting 'Mistake:' (the eleven back-filled on 2026-10-23) are counted as mistakes in status and the audit. Records are not rewritten. The text-prefix rule is documented in a code comment or doc.
`cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

Outcome-check: a reader of the status or audit output can see how many mistakes occurred, which classes and causes recur, and which prevention work was proposed. Output is not only a type or field addition.

out_of_scope: Automatically implementing the proposed prevention checks
departures: Touches several crates (data, core, cli) and has some ambiguity about 'cause', so cost, time and pass rate are worse than the reference.
